items.title: Fork into installable Claude Code plugin
items.note: Secaudit is now a one-step installable plugin with sharper, more focused security checks and new coverage for Expo, React Native, and Convex apps.

items.title: Comprehensive coverage and cited sources
items.note: Every security check is now backed by cited sources, and the audit covers the full OWASP Top 10 with new checks for cryptography, web vulnerabilities (XSS, SSRF, file uploads), and security logging.

items.title: Live CVE and advisory lookup
items.note: Version and dependency checks now look up the latest published security advisories as they run, so you're alerted to newly disclosed issues instead of relying only on a built-in list.

items.title: Dynamic verification against the running app
items.note: The audit can now optionally run your app and actively test it to confirm real vulnerabilities and filter out false alarms.

items.title: Risk-ranked scoping, finding verification, and admin-surface review
items.note: Audits now start with your highest-risk areas, can zero in on a single part of your app such as the admin area, and double-check each finding before reporting it.

items.title: Redact secrets in audit output (Snyk W007)
items.note: Security audits now mask any secrets they find in their reports instead of repeating the real values, so running an audit can't itself leak a credential into logs or transcripts.

items.title: Diff/PR-scoped audit mode
items.note: You can now point the audit at just your current branch or a pull request's changes, getting a fast, focused review of what you changed instead of the whole app.

items.title: Attack-chain construction in reports
items.note: Audit reports now connect related weaknesses into a single step-by-step attack path, so you can see how separate issues combine into a real-world risk.

items.title: Recon and coverage-gap phases
items.note: Audits now begin by mapping your app's attack surface and end with a check for anything the sweep missed, making the review more thorough.

items.title: Evidence-backed findings (anti-hallucination)
items.note: Every reported issue is now backed by a verified spot in your code and a concrete attack path, so you get fewer false alarms.

items.title: Cross-reference official Convex/Expo build skills
items.note: When auditing Convex or Expo apps, the audit now points you to the official build guides for those platforms and checks their recommended security settings.

items.title: Correct wrong CVE fix-versions in framework-versions
items.note: Version-check advice now points at genuinely patched releases; several entries previously named a version that was still vulnerable.

items.title: Remap OWASP Top 10 citations to the 2025 edition
items.note: All OWASP category references now match the current 2025 Top 10 numbering.

items.title: Update AI skill to LLM Top 10 2026 and MCP 2026-07-28 spec
items.note: AI and MCP guidance now tracks the 2026 LLM Top 10 and the current Model Context Protocol revision.

items.title: Add ChainDrop npm worm and no-CVE detection to supply-chain
items.note: Dependency checks no longer rely on advisory scanners alone, so a compromised package that was never formally reported can still be caught.

items.title: Fix dead and redirected source URLs
items.note: Repairs one dead documentation link and four that had moved.

items.title: Add 2026 Next.js middleware-bypass wave and CISA KEV entries
items.note: The version check now recognises a recent group of framework authentication flaws, including two that are known to be under active attack.

items.title: Self-checking freshness script for hardcoded versions and links
items.note: Adds a script that re-checks every version and link the skills cite, so outdated advice is caught automatically instead of drifting unnoticed.

items.title: Add prisma-security skill (Prisma, Postgres RLS, pgvector)
items.note: New checks for projects using Prisma with Postgres, including tenant isolation and vector search used by AI features.

items.title: Add better-auth-security skill
items.note: New checks for apps built with Better Auth, covering session handling, organization roles, and account linking.

items.title: Add docker-security skill
items.note: New checks for containerised projects, covering image contents, published ports, and runtime permissions.

items.title: Add python-web-security skill (FastAPI, Django)
items.note: New checks for Python backends built with FastAPI or Django.

items.title: Extend ai-integration with chat and RAG application layer
items.note: AI checks now cover chat apps end to end, including conversation history, retrieval, and how tools are given access to data.

items.title: Extend data-access, supply-chain and logging-monitoring for Python
items.note: Existing checks now recognise Python equivalents alongside the JavaScript ones.

items.title: Freshness check misses versions named as a CVE fix
items.note: The automated freshness check now also verifies versions named as a fix for a specific issue, catching outdated upgrade advice it previously skipped.

items.title: Add coverage for Nuxt, React Router, Vite and Node.js
items.note: Version checks now cover several more widely used frameworks and the Node.js runtime itself.

items.title: Extend dynamic-verification to containers
items.note: When a container is running, the audit can now confirm container findings against it instead of reporting them as suspected.

items.title: Add mcp-agent-security skill
items.note: New checks for apps that connect AI agents to external tools, covering the permissions those connections are granted.

items.title: Parallel subagent fan-out for whole-app audits
items.note: Whole-app audits now run each area in its own worker, so large projects get read thoroughly instead of sampled.

items.title: Add EPSS exploitation scoring and endoflife.date runtime EOL
items.note: Findings are now ranked by how likely an issue is to actually be exploited, and the audit flags runtimes that no longer receive security updates.

items.title: Add revenuecat-security skill (mobile IAP)
items.note: New checks for apps selling subscriptions through mobile in-app purchase.

items.title: Add Clerk coverage to auth
items.note: New checks for apps using Clerk for sign-in.

items.title: Add object-storage-security skill (R2, S3, Supabase Storage)
items.note: New checks for file and image storage, covering who can read uploaded files and for how long.

items.title: Continuous dependency monitoring for app repos
items.note: A drop-in scheduled check that watches an app's own dependencies and tells you which issues are actually being exploited, instead of listing everything that could be updated.

items.title: Close verified gaps in payments and supply-chain
items.note: Payment webhook checks now cover replayed and duplicated events, sender verification, and secret rotation; dependency checks verify lockfiles use secure download URLs.

items.title: Freshness fix-claim check pairs every CVE on a line with every fixed clause; pair with nearest CVE
items.note: The automated freshness check no longer raises a false alarm when one paragraph names fixes for two different issues.

items.title: framework-versions: add Hono, Auth.js, Drizzle, Traefik, Koa/Fastify/Elysia, TanStack Start floors and the shared image-pipeline CVE pattern
items.note: Version checks now cover several more widely used web frameworks, ORMs and proxies.

items.title: Add ci-cd-security skill: GitHub Actions pwn-requests, SHA pinning, permissions, run: injection, keyless cosign
items.note: New checks for GitHub Actions workflows, covering workflows that hand secrets to untrusted pull requests, unpinned third-party actions and over-broad token permissions.

items.title: Add cloudflare-workers-security skill: Hono (CVE-2026-24473), D1/KV/R2 bindings, wrangler secrets vs [vars]
items.note: New checks for apps deployed on Cloudflare Workers with Hono, D1, KV and R2 bindings.

items.title: Extend data-access with Drizzle (CVE-2026-39356 identifier injection, sql.raw) and SQLite/Turso/D1 file and tenancy specifics
items.note: Data-access checks now recognise Drizzle ORM and SQLite-based databases such as Turso and D1.

items.title: Add oauth-oidc-security skill: client flows (Lucia/Arctic, Sign in with X) and provider side
items.note: New checks for social sign-in and OAuth flows, on both the app side and the identity-provider side.

items.title: Add Auth.js/NextAuth coverage to auth
items.note: New checks for apps that let users sign in through NextAuth, including how linked accounts are matched.

items.title: Add proxy-trust skill: X-Forwarded-* and Host trust, forward-auth identity-header injection, Traefik CVE-2026-35051/39858, Cloudflare Access JWT verification
items.note: New checks for apps served through a reverse proxy or tunnel, covering which forwarded request details the app should believe.

items.title: Add kubernetes-security skill or docker-security section: Helm values secrets, RBAC wildcards, securityContext, hostPath, NetworkPolicy
items.note: New checks for apps deployed to Kubernetes with Helm charts, covering cluster permissions, pod settings and chart values.

items.title: Generalize payments webhook section into webhook-security: Discord Ed25519, Slack, GitHub, Svix, Telegram verification and replay
items.note: Incoming webhook checks now cover chat and developer platforms such as Discord, Slack and GitHub, not only payment providers.

items.title: Add realtime-security skill: WebSocket, SSE and long-poll auth, Origin checks (CSWSH), channel authorization, connection limits
items.note: New checks for live-updating features such as WebSockets, server-sent events and long-polling, covering who can connect and which updates they receive.

items.title: Add postgres-security skill: Drizzle RLS policies, LISTEN/NOTIFY tenant leaks, advisory locks, poolers, roles and backups
items.note: New checks for self-hosted Postgres, covering row-level security set up through Drizzle, realtime notifications and database roles.

items.title: Add discord-bot-security skill: bot tokens, intents, command permissions, role-sync hierarchy, allowedMentions, Discord OAuth identity
items.note: New checks for Discord bots and Discord sign-in, covering bot tokens, command permissions and role syncing.

items.title: Extend auth with multi-host sessions, cross-host handoff tokens and custom-domain verification
items.note: Sign-in checks now cover apps that keep users logged in across several domains, including customer-owned custom domains.

items.title: Add fivem-security skill: client-triggerable net events, replicated convars, client-script secrets, game-server credentials
items.note: New checks for FiveM game servers and the web services they connect to.

items.title: Extend cryptography with low-entropy code hashing, key-prefix lookup and AEAD binding for encrypted-at-rest secrets
items.note: Cryptography checks now cover invite and join codes, stored access keys and encrypted stored secrets such as webhook URLs.

items.title: Refresh framework-versions for advisories published since 2026-09-16 (Next.js, Hono, Fastify, Elysia, TanStack Start) and fix two redirected source links
items.note: Version-check advice now reflects the security fixes released over the past month.

items.title: Add api-surface skill: accidentally exposed backend and internal APIs, BFF open proxies, docs/introspection/debug endpoints in production, OWASP API Top 10 inventory
items.note: New checks for backend and internal services that are reachable from the internet by mistake.

items.title: Audit methodology: variant analysis after each confirmed finding and a fail-open insecure-defaults sweep
items.note: Audits now hunt for repeats of every confirmed issue elsewhere in the code and check what happens when a setting is missing.

items.title: proxy-trust grep heuristics use quoted brace globs in --include that never expand
items.note: Some search commands in the proxy checks silently matched nothing; they now find what they are meant to.

items.title: TanStack npm compromise postmortem link moved to old.tanstack.com
items.note: The source link for the May 2026 TanStack supply-chain incident points to its current home again.

items.title: Cover OpenTelemetry trace attributes leaking database usernames (CVE-2026-104872) in logging-monitoring
items.note: Logging checks now flag tracing setups that send your database account names to monitoring tools.

items.title: Nuxt blog source URL now redirects to nuxt.com/updates
items.note: The Nuxt release-announcements source link points to its current address.

items.title: Raise Next.js and React floors for the October 14 2026 advisories
items.note: Next.js and React version checks now flag the latest critical fixes.

items.title: Warn that OSV and npm audit miss vendor-only and unpublished advisories
items.note: Dependency checks no longer treat an empty advisory lookup as proof a package is safe.

items.title: Add a rich-text-security skill for editors, docx import and sanitizers
items.note: New checks for rich-text editors, document import and HTML sanitizing.

items.title: Add a multi-tenant-isolation hub skill
items.note: New checks for keeping each tenant's data separate across caches, jobs, domains and search.

items.title: Audit a target repo's committed AI-agent config and agent CI actions
items.note: Audits now review the AI-agent settings, hooks and MCP servers a project ships.

items.title: Audit must vet project agents as untrusted before delegating to them
items.note: Audits treat a project's bundled helper agents with appropriate caution.

items.title: Cover Drizzle write-path risks: mass assignment, unscoped writes, races
items.note: Deeper Drizzle ORM checks for unsafe writes and race conditions.

items.title: Cover modern browser defenses and DOM navigation and postMessage sinks
items.note: New browser-side checks for content security policy, Trusted Types and cross-window messaging.

items.title: Cover Next.js 16 caching, Server Action key and image config risks
items.note: New checks for cached per-user data, Server Actions and image settings in modern React apps.

items.title: Deepen fivem-security: server.cfg convars, game-event vetoes, exports
items.note: Deeper FiveM server checks for server settings, game events and cross-resource calls.
